- [1909] Ettore Bugatti founded Automobiles E. Bugatti in Molsheim, France, producing high-performance sports cars.

- [1930s] Bugatti faced financial difficulties due to the economic downturn and changing consumer preferences.
- [World War II] Bugatti's factory in Molsheim was occupied by German forces, halting car production. Ettore Bugatti fled to Italy, and the factory was heavily damaged.
- [1947] Ettore Bugatti passed away at the age of 66.
- [1950s] Bugatti was sold to Hispano-Suiza due to financial difficulties.
- [1960s-70s] Ownership of Bugatti changed hands multiple times, including to Roland Bugatti and Romano Artioli.
- [1991-1995] Romano Artioli launched the Bugatti EB110, a high-performance supercar.
- [1998] The Volkswagen Group acquired the Bugatti brand.
- [2005] The Bugatti Veyron, a high-performance supercar, was unveiled.
- [2016] The Bugatti Chiron, a successor to the Veyron, was unveiled, boasting a top speed of over 300 mph.
